# Tatiyanānātitthiya Sutta (Ud 6.6 (PTS Ud 70))

**ID:** Ud 6.6 (PTS Ud 70)  
**Section:** Udāna (ud)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Tatiyanānātitthiya Sutta  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0503m.mul5.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0503m.mul5.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In this sutta, wanderers of various outside schools fall into heated disputation concerning the nature of the self (*attā*), the world (*loko*), pleasure, and pain [Levman 2014]. In particular, they debate whether the self and the world are created by oneself or by another (*sayamkato ca paramkato ca attā ca loko ca*) [Levman 2014]. The Buddha encapsulates the futility of these sectarian views in an inspired utterance (*udāna* / *gāthā*), observing that people are bound by the notions that "I am the doer" (*ahaṅkāra*) or that "another is the doer" (*paraṅkāra*) [Levman 2014].
